changes.summary: The MambaPool temporal-state copy previously gathered every selected source slot into one temporary tensor before writing the destination slots, so one checkpoint copy could spike transient GPU memory. The gather is now chunked against a 64 MiB budget with a one-slot floor, bounding the temporary allocation to a full state slot at least; small copies remain a single batched assignment and source and destination slot sets must stay disjoint. Copied and untouched slots were checked exact.

validation.review: Independent public review of the runtime change is clean; the focused public tests were 3 tests plus 2 subtests in total, run on the public tree before this record.
validation.rtx_a4000: Transient gather peak measured over four copies: 576 to 144 MiB on the 27B state shape and 216 to 54 MiB on the Flash-Next shape; copied and untouched slots exact.
validation.rtx_pro_6000: Both profiles, run separately, served four correct answers with natural stops and 9,344 GPU-cached tokens per request with zero host/storage reuse; Flash-Next served all four from one prefill (37,376 cached tokens).
validation.caveats: The concurrent 27B requests entered prefill separately, so no multi-slot 27B gather was exercised in one batch there. No RTX PRO 6000 peak-memory measurement, no KV-capacity or DFlash host-RAM savings claim, no broad qualification or throughput campaign, and no speed claim.

validation.image_gpu_serving: Recorded 2026-11-03. The exact image at the digest above booted the public tiered Flash-Next profile with native NEXTN on an RTX PRO 6000, with NIXL, 32 GB HiCache and medium reasoning effort, configured with a limit of four running requests and 24 Mamba slots; the limit is a concurrency ceiling, not observed simultaneous traffic. The smoke sent one generation request and then one parallel-tool-call request. Health answered 200; streaming generation returned exactly READY with a natural stop and DONE, and the parallel-tool-call fixture emitted lookup_alpha with key=ALPHA and lookup_bravo with key=BRAVO as valid JSON with two distinct IDs, no prose, finish_reason tool_calls and DONE. These are tool-call emission checks, not execution of the declared dummy tools. The native everyday service was restored afterwards and passed the same two requests. This is a bounded generation and tool smoke: no benchmark, no throughput or timing claim, and the dated two-profile and A4000 evidence above is unchanged.
